overall: Atlanta is tracking a warm, humid afternoon with the current temperature already at 87.8°F as of 13:20 ET, matching the running daily maximum. Despite a broken cloud deck (~62%) and a 40% chance of afternoon thunderstorms beginning after 1 PM, positive warming velocity (+5.4°F/hr) indicates the temperature has not yet peaked. The day is running hotter than several models initially anticipated, with ECMWF (83.8°F) and NBM (86.0°F) already busted low.
forecast_obs_notes: Model spread is significant: ECMWF and NBM are already below observed temps and effectively out of play, leaving HRRR (89.8°F) as the most credible remaining NWP guidance and closely aligned with the NWS official forecast of near 89°F. The META probability distribution concentrates probability in the 88–91°F range (~52% combined), with the 90–91°F and 88–89°F buckets tied at 26.2% each, suggesting modest upside risk above the NWS headline.
max_temp_prediction: With the current temp at 87.8°F, still-positive velocity, and the predicted peak not until ~14:30 ET, additional warming of 1–2°F is plausible before the peak. The primary cap on further gains is convective initiation — early thunderstorm development after 1 PM could rapidly halt the warmup through cloud shading and outflow cooling, while a delayed storm holds the path open to the HRRR-projected ~89.8°F. Balancing HRRR guidance, NWS consensus near 89°F, and the storm timing risk, confidence is moderate that the daily high lands in the 89–90°F range.
